elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to each Party.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 states that “each Party's aggregate liability” is subject to the cap.

elements.element: Fees paid are included in the fee-based cap calculation.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly includes “fees paid.”

elements.element: Fees payable are included in the fee-based cap calculation.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly includes fees “payable.”

elements.element: The fee-based cap calculation uses the twelve months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 measures fees in “the twelve months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: USD 1,000,000 is an alternative cap amount.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly includes “USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the twelve-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses the required “greater of” formulation.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 provides that “neither Party” is liable for indirect damages, subject to the Excluded Claims carve-outs.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 provides that “neither Party” is liable for consequential damages, subject to the Excluded Claims carve-outs.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 excludes all Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data-protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Data-protection breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 excludes all Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Security breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 excludes all Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 excludes all Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 excludes all Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 excludes all Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 excludes all Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property as an Excluded Claim, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 states that Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under the Agreement “is not damages and is not limited by this Section.”

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to each Party.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies the same cap formulation to “each Party's aggregate liability.”

elements.element: The liability cap is no less than twelve months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses twelve months of fees as one branch of a greater-of formula, so the resulting cap cannot be lower than that amount.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3 and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3 and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3 and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3 and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

result.reason: The operative language implements the complete preferred position: a mutual greater-of cap, mutual damages exclusion, all required uncapped carve-outs, and the payment-obligation treatment. It also meets or exceeds the fallback floor. The changes are confined to correcting the cap, restoring the Excluded Claims exception, and broadening the payment carve-out. Drafting quality is reduced because Section 21.1 uses lowercase “fees” even though the original clause appears to use the defined term “Fees,” creating avoidable ambiguity.
